rules.night: A night is one run_start and the records after it up to the next one; the run resumes each night. Its date is the date it started, on the clock of the card's host.
rules.classes: Coverage is evidence about the thing that ran. A slice swept on one RTL tree says nothing about another, so a tile item is counted per RTL tree, and a host item per host tree and compiler, because no tile computes it. A changed tree starts a new class from nothing, and nothing is summed across classes. How a run that did not record its tree is placed is the report's rule, and the class's label says which.
rules.groups: Within a class the items are in up to three groups, each counted over its own items and spaces so that a group joining a class does not move the others' figures: the base items; the wide-format items (fp64, fp128 and fp256), which exist only in a tool built against the pinned MPFR; and the routine items (a routine of the maths library compiled to a program, run on the tile against MPFR, one item a routine). A class's total is over all its groups. Each item names the format it computes in; a conversion names both ends.
rules.estimate: ESTIMATE, not a measurement. For an item not yet fully covered in a current class: its gain over the class's last 3 nights (fewer if the class is younger), divided by the nights in that window, is its rate a night; the nights left are the remaining indices over that rate, rounded up; the date counts that many days after the newest night, assuming a night every day. It does not know of a skipped night, or that items finishing free time for the rest.
rules.card_time: Time on the card is the report's: the union of the battery and sweep legs' intervals on the card images, skipped legs and the host pool's legs left out. The wall span runs from the first record to the last and includes the days between nights.

rates.rule: Per night, from that night's own records: the card's throughput by op and format, in cases a second on one tile. A row is an (image, op, format, level); it is made of the night's sweep slices that ran on a tile of the card (reach tile, level exhaustive or hard, status pass) and of nothing else: the class level (one case a call), the host reach (the CPU) and the random items are left out, and `left_out` counts them and every other leg that is not in a row, by reason. A rate is the slice's own, its cases over its whole duration with the soak process's start and the host's oracle in it, so it is the pipeline's pace and not the tile's alone. A case is one element through the op; a hard item's cases are the ones its tool compared, its skipped slots left out. `all` is the image's slices pooled and `tiles` each tile's ([slices, cases, median, least, most], cases a second); `sum` adds the tiles' medians, least and most (bounds, not measured quad rates). `card` is the night's probe rate with the oracle off for the same op and format, per tile, and its ratio to `all`'s median; null where no probe ran that night, never a zero. `from` names the catalog ops pooled in a row.
